how_to_read: One row per decision-blocking question. 'What we already have' records only what an official page or this repository establishes. 'What is missing' names the gap precisely. 'How to discover it' is the concrete action that would close it. 'Default if unanswered' is what the site does anyway, so nothing waits forever.

questions.question: Which product was each of the five submitted links actually meant to reach?
questions.have: The observed destination of all five links, captured 2026-11-17. All five tokens are 9 characters; an ASIN is defined as 10 characters, so the tokens themselves are not the identifier.
questions.missing: The account owner's statement of intent for each link. A redirect destination is an observation, not evidence of intent.
questions.discover: Ask the owner to state the intended ASIN - or at least the intended product - for each of the five links. Cross-check against Associates reports once the account is enrolled.
questions.blocks: Every product page, every comparison row, and the chooser in DS-06.
questions.default: The intended-ASIN field stays blank on every row and the site publishes only the observed destination, labelled as observed.

questions.question: Are the two thermometers in scope for this site, or are they a separate project?
questions.have: Three of the five links land in the Air Fryers browse node (17659096011) and two land in Meat, under Thermometers & Timers (289810). The whole published site is currently built around a single air-fryer category.
questions.missing: The owner's decision on the site's scope.
questions.discover: An explicit choice on the Choose a path page: one kitchen site with two pillars, an air-fryer-only site, or two separate sites.
questions.blocks: The navigation, the category pages, the brand name, and DS-01, DS-10, DS-15 and DS-16.
questions.default: Path A - one kitchen site with two category pillars - because it is the only option that keeps all five submitted products on the same domain.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled, approved and in good standing?
questions.have: The requirements are public: an application is reviewed before the account can earn, and an account that refers no sale in 180 days can be closed for dormancy.
questions.missing: Any evidence about this specific account. The brief supplies a tracking ID but nothing confirms the account's state.
questions.discover: Log in to Associates Central and read the account status panel. Only the account holder can do this.
questions.blocks: Any tagged outbound link, any commission, and the entire monetisation premise.
questions.default: No monetised link is published. The site stays a factual product-information site with untagged, clearly-labelled links to the official listings.

questions.question: Is the supplied tracking tag valid for this account?
questions.have: A tracking tag appears in the brief. The Creators API documentation shows a partner tag as a required request parameter, and the Operating Agreement requires links to use the tagged formats Amazon provides.
questions.missing: Any confirmation that this tag belongs to this account and is accepted.
questions.discover: Compare the tag against the account's own tag list in Associates Central, or observe whether a link built with it reports a click.
questions.blocks: Every outbound product link that would carry a tag.
questions.default: No tagged link is published until the tag is confirmed in the account itself.

questions.question: What is the exact Special Link format this account should use?
questions.have: The Operating Agreement requires links to use the special tagged link formats Amazon provides. Commission is paid on purchases made through a Special Link.
questions.missing: The actual link string for this account, which is generated inside Associates Central or SiteStripe.
questions.discover: Generate one link for one product in the enrolled Associates workflow, confirm where it lands, and confirm that it reports in the account before scaling to the rest.
questions.blocks: Any claim that an outbound link is monetised, and the 'replace ambiguous outbound links with validated Special Links' requirement.
questions.default: Links point at the official /dp/ listing URL and are labelled as plain links to Amazon, not as affiliate links.

questions.question: Does a link.amazon hop count as a Redirecting Link under the Commission Income Statement?
questions.have: The Commission Income Statement defines a Qualifying Purchase as beginning with a click through a Special Link, and describes sessions that end when the customer clicks through a Special Link that is not yours.
questions.missing: Whether an intermediate link.amazon hop is treated as the Associate's Special Link or as a redirect that terminates the session. That is determined by Amazon's systems, not by reading the policy text.
questions.discover: Test one link in the enrolled account and read the resulting report. Unresolvable without an enrolled account.
questions.blocks: The decision to keep the supplied short links or replace them.
questions.default: The compliance status of the supplied short links stays recorded as unresolved, and the site does not assert that they are either valid or invalid.

questions.question: Which product values may be displayed, and from which source?
questions.have: Earlier sessions recorded that Program Policies restrict displaying price, star ratings and review counts outside an Amazon-served link or the Creators API, and remediated the repository accordingly. The Creators API is the documented route for price and offer data.
questions.missing: A Creators API credential for this account, without which no price or offer value can be lawfully displayed here.
questions.discover: Obtain Creators API credentials in the enrolled account and read the GetItems OffersV2 responses for the confirmed ASINs.
questions.blocks: Any price comparison, any rating column, and the 'analyzes pricing, reviews, competition' part of the brief.
questions.default: Those cells stay blank with the reason printed in the cell. No value is inferred from an observed listing page.

questions.question: Which marketplace and locale is the site written for?
questions.have: The five links all resolve to amazon.com. Commission rates are published per marketplace and per category.
questions.missing: Confirmation that amazon.com is the intended marketplace. The account owner is located in Singapore, which is a different Associates marketplace with its own rate table.
questions.discover: An owner decision, checked against the marketplace the Associates account is actually registered in.
questions.blocks: Which commission table applies, which currency any displayed value would use, and which links are valid.
questions.default: Treat amazon.com as the marketplace, because that is where all five links land, and flag the mismatch between that and the owner's location.

questions.question: Where will product photography come from, and on what licence?
questions.have: Program Content includes images, and it specifically excludes product information relating to any site other than the Amazon Site.
questions.missing: Any photograph the site owns or is licensed to publish, and a decision on who takes them.
questions.discover: Either the owner supplies photographs they took, or the site ships without product photography.
questions.default: No product photography. The design carries the page with typography, colour and layout instead, which is honest and also faster to load.

questions.question: Is there analytics and Search Console access?
questions.have: Nothing. No analytics property and no verified Search Console property is recorded anywhere in the repository.
questions.missing: Both, plus the consent basis for measuring outbound clicks.
questions.discover: Create the properties, verify the domain, and install the measurement before the next article is written.
questions.blocks: Every 'measure whether anyone arrives' step, and DS-18 and DS-19.
questions.default: Topics are chosen by judgement and labelled as working hypotheses, never as measured demand.

questions.question: Who writes the articles, and how often?
questions.have: Nothing about authorship or cadence is recorded, and no byline exists on any published page.
questions.missing: A named author and a cadence the owner can sustain.
questions.discover: An owner decision. Set the cadence to what survives a bad month, not a good week.
questions.blocks: The bylines in DS-13, the clusters in DS-16, and any claim of a publishing schedule.
questions.default: No cadence is claimed. Articles publish when they are ready, and the site does not promise a schedule.

questions.question: What is the lawful basis for counting outbound clicks?
questions.have: The brief defines five events to record and asks for a privacy-preserving counter and a self-hosted endpoint.
questions.missing: A privacy notice for the site, a decision on retention, and a decision on whether any identifier is stored.
questions.discover: Write the privacy notice and decide retention before the counter goes live. Aggregate counts with no personal identifier is the low-risk default.
questions.blocks: Turning on click measurement, and DS-18.
questions.default: The counter stays off. Aggregate page counts only, with no per-visitor identifier stored.

questions.question: Has the brand name and voice been settled?
questions.have: A design brief and a set of editorial rules exist in the repository from earlier sessions, and one earlier session recorded a brand decision.
questions.missing: Confirmation that the current brand and voice are the ones the owner wants, and that they fit a site that now spans two categories.
questions.discover: An owner decision on the Choose a path page, since the brand should follow the scope decision in 5B-Q02.
questions.blocks: The masthead, the domain choice, and the visual overhaul.
questions.default: Keep the existing brand and voice rather than renaming mid-build; renaming after the scope decision is cheaper than renaming before it.

questions.question: Will anyone actually test these products hands-on?
questions.have: The FTC's guidance is that an endorsement must reflect the honest experience of the endorser and that a reviewer should not imply experience they do not have.
questions.missing: Someone with the products in front of them. Nothing in the repository records a hands-on test.
questions.discover: An owner decision; if the products cannot be tested, the site must say so plainly instead of implying it.
questions.blocks: Any review framing, and the 'what the appliance is like to live with' requirement.
questions.default: The site writes from listing facts and says so. It never implies that a product has been used, and it never invents an experience of using one.
